edges.reason: Parameter a is consumed as the first operand of safeAdd.
Parameter b is consumed as the second operand of safeAdd.
safeAdd performs the unsigned addition a + b that is the overflow-sensitive operation.
Parameter a is consumed as the first operand of safeSub.
Parameter b is consumed as the second operand of safeSub.
Parameter a is consumed as the first operand of safeMul.
Parameter b is consumed as the second operand of safeMul.
safeMul performs the unsigned multiplication a * b that is the overflow-sensitive operation.
Parameter a is consumed as the dividend of safeDiv.
Parameter b is consumed as the divisor of safeDiv.
The _newOwner parameter is stored into the newOwner state variable.
The onlyOwner modifier compares msg.sender against the owner state variable before executing the body.
msg.sender is the value checked by the onlyOwner guard on transferOwnership.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender == newOwner, so the newOwner state variable gates execution.
msg.sender is compared against newOwner in the acceptOwnership guard.
acceptOwnership resets the newOwner state variable to address(0).
acceptOwnership writes the owner state variable with the value of newOwner.
The Owned constructor assigns the privileged owner role from msg.sender.
The Owned constructor writes owner = msg.sender.
tokenOwner is used as the lookup key into the balances mapping in balanceOf.
balanceOf reads the balances state mapping.
totalSupply reads the _totalSupply state variable.
totalSupply reads balances[address(0)] as part of the returned value.
The to parameter is used as the credit key in the balances mapping in transfer.
The tokens parameter is the amount debited and credited in transfer.
msg.sender indexes balances for the debited account in transfer.
transfer reads balances for both the sender and the recipient.
transfer writes the updated sender and recipient entries into the balances mapping.
transfer delegates the sender balance decrement to safeSub.
transfer delegates the recipient balance increment to safeAdd.
The spender parameter is the inner key written in the allowed mapping.
The tokens parameter is the allowance value written in approve without checks.
msg.sender is the outer key written into the allowed mapping in approve.
approve writes the allowed state mapping.
The from parameter is the account debited in transferFrom.
The to parameter is the account credited in transferFrom.
The tokens parameter is the amount moved in transferFrom.
msg.sender is the spender whose allowance is decremented in transferFrom.
transferFrom reads and writes the balances state mapping.
transferFrom reads and writes the allowed state mapping.
transferFrom calls safeSub for both the balance and allowance decrements.
transferFrom calls safeAdd for the recipient balance increment.
transferFrom writes the updated balances back into the mapping.
tokenOwner is the outer key of the allowed lookup in allowance.
spender is the inner key of the allowed lookup in allowance.
allowance reads the allowed state mapping.
The spender parameter is both the allowance key and the callee of the external call.
The tokens parameter is the allowance written and forwarded to receiveApproval.
The attacker-controlled data bytes are forwarded into the external receiveApproval call.
msg.sender is written as the allowance owner and passed as the from argument of the callback.
approveAndCall writes the allowed state mapping.
approveAndCall makes an untrusted external call to the caller-supplied spender contract, allowing reentrant execution.
approveAndCall updates the allowed mapping before returning success.
The caller-supplied tokenAddress is cast to ERC20Interface and called externally.
The tokens parameter is forwarded as the amount of the external transfer call.
transferAnyERC20Token is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier checking owner.
msg.sender is compared against owner by the onlyOwner modifier.
transferAnyERC20Token performs an untrusted external call on an arbitrary token contract, enabling reentrancy.
The reentrant receiveApproval callback can re-enter approveAndCall or approve and mutate the allowed allowance state.
The external ERC20 transfer call happens while owner is read, letting a malicious token re-enter owner-gated functions.
